title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.281). M is an Azumaya algebra over a base scheme S; from the matrix normalisation in the margin it is of rank 4, i.e. locally M_2(O_S). G(M) is its unit group scheme.

Data:
- ε1 = 1+N1 is a unipotent section with N1² = 0.
- ρ, σ are invertible sections linked by formula (77): σ = -ε1^{-1}ρ, i.e. ρ+σ = N1ρ = -N1σ.

Hypotheses:
- (2°) 1, ρ^{-1}, N1 (equivalently 1, σ^{-1}, N1) are linearly independent on each fibre. The margin rewrites this with ε1 in place of N1.
- (3°) Tr(N1ρ) is invertible.
- A marginal NB notes that 2° is a consequence of 3°, up to normalisation.

First observation. ρ^{-1}ε1ρ = -σ^{-1}ρ = σ^{-1}ε1σ. So int(ρ^{-1})ε1 = int(σ^{-1})ε1 =: ε0 = 1+N0, and conversely int(ρ)ε0 = int(σ)ε0 = ε1.

One-parameter subgroups. Set ε_i(λ) = 1+λN_i (additive one-parameter subgroups, G_a → G(M)) and L_i = ε_i(G_a). Then ρL0ρ^{-1} = σL0σ^{-1} = L1. B0 is the normaliser of L0 (marked 'Borel').

The subgroup B'0. B'0 is a subgroup scheme of B0 cut out by condition (74), not visible on this page. It sits in an exact sequence 1 → L0 → B'0 → G_m → 1 (det), and every u in B'0 satisfies u N0 u^{-1} = det(u) N0, i.e. u ε0(λ) u^{-1} = ε0(det(u) λ). Locally, with N0 = E12, this forces u = [[a,b],[0,1]]. So B'0 is the 'ax+b' affine group, a semidirect product G_a ⋊ G_m.

The key map. Grothendieck considers the morphism B'0 → G(M) × G(M) × E^1 given by u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], det u). The next page states that it lands in X_{ρ,σ}, the scheme of solutions (ξ, η, μ) of the simultaneous equations (33)–(35) (the 'loop equation' system relative to fixed ρ, σ). It induces an isomorphism (79) B'0 ≅ X_{ρ,σ}. Hence the scholie: 'by transport of structure' the solution scheme acquires a group structure.

Marginal normal form. ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]] and ρ = [[0,λ],[a,b]]. Then N1ρ = [[0,0],[0,λ]], so Tr N1ρ = λ, normalised to λ = 1. Then σ = -ε1^{-1}ρ and ρ+σ = diag(0,1) = N1ρ.

Purpose. Within the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (the relation for loops around the three punctures of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, in a rank-2 / Azumaya setting), this computes the solution scheme of the loop equations for fixed ρ, σ in the unipotent-degenerate case. It identifies that scheme as a torsor under / isomorphic to a Borel-type affine group via commutators.
errors: The text says 'de sorte que B0 s'insère dans une suite exacte 1→L0→B0→G_m→1'. For the full normaliser B0 (a Borel, of dimension 3 in GL2) this is false on dimensional grounds. It holds for the subgroup B'0 cut out by (74) (u = [[a,b],[0,1]]), so 'B0' should read B'0 here.

The interlinear insertion read as 'centralisateur de ε0' (machine transcription) conflicts with the stated property u(N0) = det(u)N0. The centraliser would give u(N0) = N0. Either the insertion is misread or it is a slip; B'0 is not the centraliser.
Marginal matrix: with ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]] and ρ = [[0,1],[a,b]], one gets σ = -ε1^{-1}ρ = [[0,-1],[-a,1-b]]. The margin appears to write +a in the (2,1) entry, a sign slip or misreading.

ideas.what: Conjugating the unipotent ε1 by ρ^{-1} or σ^{-1} gives the same unipotent ε0 when σ = -ε1^{-1}ρ
ideas.modern_name: elementary conjugation identity in GL2 / quaternion algebras

ideas.what: Solution scheme of the loop equations for fixed (ρ,σ) is isomorphic, via u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det u), to the 'ax+b' subgroup of the normaliser of the root group L0, hence carries a group structure
ideas.modern_name: parametrisation of a fibre of a character-variety-type relation scheme by a Borel subgroup (torsor structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; analogous computations appear in the study of SL2/GL2 character varieties of the thrice-punctured sphere and Fricke–Klein trace coordinates

ideas.what: Normal form of the data in M_2: ε1 lower unipotent, ρ = [[0,1],[a,b]], normalised so that Tr N1ρ = 1

missed.claim: In the unipotent-degenerate case of the loop equation over an Azumaya algebra of rank 4, the scheme X_{ρ,σ} of solutions is identified with the affine group G_a ⋊ G_m via commutators with ρ and σ. This gives it an unexpected group structure 'by transport'. It is an explicit, scheme-theoretic computation over an arbitrary base (Azumaya rather than split M_2) that does not seem to be written down in this form.
missed.quote: considérons le morphisme B'_0 → G(M)×G(M)×E^1, u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det(u))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor but clean description of a degenerate stratum of a rank-2 character-variety-type scheme over a general base. It is of modest interest for relative character varieties of P^1 minus 3 points with unipotent monodromy.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially routine linear-algebra computation in GL2 / quaternion algebras, part of a long working computation. The commutator-parametrisation of the solution scheme by a Borel-type group is neat but not something a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: The exact sequence line reads '1 → L0 ↪ B0 →det G_m → 1' in the image, but mathematically it must concern B'0.
The interlinear insertion under 'B'0 le sous-schéma en groupes' appears to read something like '...en termes de ε0' rather than clearly 'centralisateur de ε0'; uncertain.
Margin σ matrix: (2,1) entry should be -a if ρ = [[0,1],[a,b]] and ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]].
The first line likely reads 'supposons de plus (2°) 1, ρ, σ ... lin. indép. sur chaque fibre', with the corrected alternatives '1, ρ^{-1}, N1' and '1, σ^{-1}, N1' written below.
